name: DroidClaw
vibe_summary: DroidClaw turns old Android phones into autonomous AI agents that read the screen via accessibility trees and tap, type, and swipe through ADB until a plain-English goal is done. Its killer trick is delegating tasks to on-device apps like ChatGPT or Gemini — no API keys needed, it just uses apps like a human would.

overview_markdown:
DroidClaw is an open-source AI agent that turns Android phones — including old, spare devices — into autonomous operators. You give it a goal in plain English, and it runs a **perception → reasoning → action** loop: it dumps the accessibility tree via ADB, parses the XML into interactive UI elements, diffs against the previous screen to detect changes, optionally captures a screenshot, then decides whether to tap, type, swipe, or launch an app. It repeats this cycle (up to a step budget) until the goal is complete.

The standout capability is **API-free delegation**: DroidClaw can open the ChatGPT, Gemini, or Google Search apps on the device itself, submit a query, and bring the result back — using the apps exactly as a human would, with no API keys required. The project ships an Android APK (currently v0.5.3), a web dashboard, scheduled goals via QStash, and a documented set of 26 actions with failure recovery and a pairing flow.

Compared to OpenClaw, DroidClaw is a specialist rather than a generalist: it focuses entirely on mobile UI automation rather than being a broad personal assistant platform. Recent commits show active development around session management, scheduled goals, and dashboard reliability, though the project is still pre-1.0 with visible bug-fixing churn. Security hardening (sandboxing, permission scoping) is not prominently documented, so it carries meaningful operational risk given it has full control of a device.
